title: Help flag behavior
description: The brief defines no help option. Options weighed: treat --help and -h as unknown options (exit 2), or add a help flag exiting 0.

options.label: Add a help flag that exits 0

title: Invalid UTF-8 input
description: The brief's rejection list is exhaustive and omits invalid UTF-8. Options: reject with exit 3, or read bytes as encoding/csv does.

options.label: Do not reject; read as encoding/csv reads

title: Two-decimal rule for integer mean and median
description: Integer sum, min, max are plain integers, but run.sh A1 shows integer mean and median as 1012.50. Options: two places for mean and median of both numeric types, or integers only when exact.

options.label: Mean and median always two places

title: Column name matching
description: Options: exact case-sensitive match on trimmed header names, or case-insensitive match.

title: Foundation story carries no covers or accepts
description: BUILD-001 is infrastructure but must be covered by exactly one story, while a foundational story carries no covers. Planned the foundation as ARCHITECTURE.md and gave BUILD-001 to a separate module-build story that proves the build.
system_choice: BUILD-001 is covered by module-build; foundation carries neither covers nor accepts.

title: Valid single-file invocation behavior in the Run skeleton
description: Options were: return 0 with no output, or return a non-success code with a 'not implemented' diagnostic. I chose 0 with no output because exit 1 means the file cannot be read and the contract has no code for unimplemented work. Profiling stories will replace this path. Is that acceptable, or should the skeleton fail until profiling lands?

title: Blank lines
description: encoding/csv skips blank lines. Reader makes them explicit as empty records when the header has one column, so an empty value in a single-column file counts as a row and a null. In multi-column files blank lines are still skipped. Is that acceptable, or should blank lines in multi-column files be rejected as ragged?
